title: Government Structure Quiz
description: Quiz on Nepal's separation of powers, institutional roles, and accountability mechanisms.

questions.question: Which branch is primarily responsible for interpreting the Constitution?
questions.explanation: The judiciary interprets the Constitution, with the Supreme Court at the apex.

questions.question: The House of Representatives and the National Assembly together form which institution?
questions.explanation: Both houses constitute the bicameral Federal Parliament.

questions.question: Select all mechanisms that provide legislative oversight of the executive.
questions.explanation: Legislative oversight includes questioning, approving budgets, and committee inquiries; judicial writs are judicial, not legislative.

questions.question: True or False: The President exercises day-to-day executive administration independently of the Council of Ministers.
questions.explanation: Day-to-day executive authority rests with the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers; the President's role is largely ceremonial.

questions.question: Which committee stage outcome most directly influences amendment incorporation into a bill?
questions.explanation: Committee referral reports recommend amendments that may be adopted in subsequent readings.

questions.question: Which instrument allows courts to invalidate an unconstitutional executive regulation?
questions.explanation: Judicial review invalidates unconstitutional regulations or acts.

questions.question: Which factor best reflects 'checks and balances'?
options: Mutual limitation and oversight among branches
questions.explanation: Checks and balances involve mutual oversight preventing concentration of power.

questions.question: Which statement about inter-branch coordination in complex policy areas is most accurate?
options: Effective coordination complements checks while improving implementation
Only the judiciary can initiate coordination
questions.explanation: Coordination complements checks by enabling coherent implementation while maintaining oversight.

questions.question: Select all components that deepen understanding of Government Structure Quiz.
options: Irrelevant myths unrelated to the topic
questions.explanation: Core concepts, applicable frameworks, and practical examples build robust understanding; unrelated myths do not.

questions.question: Case studies help apply abstract concepts to real situations.
questions.explanation: Applying concepts in realistic contexts strengthens comprehension and recall.

questions.question: Which study approach most improves retention of key ideas?
questions.explanation: Active recall and practice yield better retention than passive reading or cramming.

questions.question: What is a practical way to connect Government Structure Quiz to real-world decisions?
options: Relate concepts to local news or policies
questions.explanation: Linking concepts to current events and local policies improves understanding and relevance.

questions.question: Select good strategies to evaluate claims about this topic.
options: Rely solely on anonymous social posts
Look for credible data and context
questions.explanation: Verifying against primary sources, mandates, and credible data yields more reliable conclusions.

questions.question: Which house of Parliament primarily represents provinces and special groups?
questions.explanation: The National Assembly (Upper House) represents provinces and special groups.

questions.question: Select instruments that exemplify judicial checks on the executive.
questions.explanation: Courts use writ jurisdiction and judicial review; appropriations and committee inquiries are legislative.

questions.question: True or False: The President exercises executive powers independently in day-to-day administration.
questions.explanation: Day-to-day executive authority rests with the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers.
